preceding_messages.text: For the initial phase, each of the six proposed sites will log hourly air-temperature, wind speed/direction, barometric pressure, and cumulative rainfall, recorded in a bound logbook with timestamp, observer initials, sky-condition code, and instrument serial number; before the first hourly entry the temperature probe is cross-checked against a NIST-traceable reference thermometer to confirm it sits within ±0.2 °C. To guard against a concrete failure—systematic thermal bias from mounting the sensor on a sun-facing concrete ledge, which in a mid-July afternoon could inflate readings by 3–5 °C relative to true ambient and corrupt the weekly trend—I require the Stevenson screen to hang at least 1.5 m from any vertical surface, with a 360° open-sky view verified by a simple horizon sketch logged at installation. Each Saturday's compiled summary will be compared against the nearest national (NOAA/NCDC) station, and any residual offset beyond combined instrument uncertainty (±0.5 °C) will trigger a recalibration entry rather than a silent correction.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt your 1.5 m Stevenson standoff, the horizon-sketch verification, and the ±0.5 °C recalibration trigger verbatim; they close the two most probable temperature-integrity holes. For the missing-data gap you haven't yet named, a missed hour is logged "MISSING" (never interpolated) and three consecutive gaps trigger a formal site-replacement review; each station must also sit ≥50 m from a paved roadway so exhaust heat and tire aerosol cannot bias the barometer or truncate anemometer readings. The concrete failure this guards against: placing the cup anemometer on the south face of a two-storey roof embeds it in a chimney wake that at 2 m s⁻¹ true speed—a neighbourhood-gust regime—under-reads by 20–30 %, so the mast must clear every obstruction by at least twice its height in all azimuths, verified with the same horizon-sketch you specified. The weekly public report will therefore carry a per-site data-completeness percentage, and any site below 62 % completeness (≈90 % of available hours) is flagged "provisional" in the bulletin rather than silently smoothed into the trend.
